title: Uncle Joe the songwriter and family background
summary: Uncle Joe wrote songs including the Axe Man piece; a grandfather played cello; family from Portugal and France.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Tell me now about your uncle.

Oh, my Uncle Joe. Yeah, he was a killer. He wrote some songs around the turn of the century. Uh, yeah, he used to have some copies somewhere. I remember, in particular one time, they'd write up in a newspaper about him. He, um, around the turn of the century, around the first war, something like that. There was a series of murders in New Orleans. And these people were bludgeoning to death with an axe. Uh, and he wrote a song called The Axe Man Blooms. I don't know where he got the title from, because I don't know who would buy the song. But, uh, and at the time they used to sing the sheet music at the dime stores in town. That's how they would hawk it, you know. You'd go down and you'd ask Dave Frank or somebody, a fellow named Frank Arena, there'd be a lady piano player sitting in the McCrory's, uh, Woolworths, and you'd say, would you play this for me? And sheet music was a big thing in those days, because everybody played a little piano at home. And they'd sing a chorus for you, really, and whether you liked it or not, I mean, if you like it, you'd buy it. And, uh, Uncle Joe wrote, uh, well, quite a few tunes. I just don't recall many of them, but, uh, and he was acquainted with a lot of musicians, you know. Did you know him?

Yeah, he died about, uh, he died about, uh, ten, twelve years ago. He was no, uh, uh, no versatile musician, but he'd played the piano by ear, and he could manage to put a few notes down on paper, you see. But he, uh, I guess he had written and recorded many, many songs. Uh, Gene Austin recorded some of his songs, and, uh, the sister trio that came out of New Orleans, the Basel Sisters, you know, they're from New Orleans. As a matter of fact, he managed them for a while. But I didn't have any association with him, I mean, uh, as the music went, because, uh, I didn't know about him too well, or, too much, and, uh, except that he used to come pop a bunch of sheet music on my sister's piano every now and then, you know. Mother's the only one I care for now, and, uh, stuff like that. I said, where'd these old songs come from? I just wondered if my sister kept some of them.
Did you have any other music in your family at all?

Not that I recall. I had a, uh, grandfather, I think it was, played in the Paris Symphony, cello. That's all I can, uh, that's all I can, uh, that's all I can find. That's all I've been able to, you know, determine. My people are from, uh, some are from, uh, Portugal. And, uh, my mother's people are from France. And, uh, it's a little hard. Not too many of them are over here.
